topics.summary: HarborRelay brings the volume’s mechanisms together in a separate multi-file application. It accepts one length-prefixed request per connection, computes a bounded integer sum, returns a framed result, and releases the connection. It has explicit admission capacity, a fixed worker count, a request deadline beginning at acceptance, and a stop path that does not depend on another client arriving.

topics.title: C.1 Requirements and acceptance contract
topics.summary: The wire format is four unsigned length bytes in network order followed by at most 4096 payload bytes. An empty payload is a valid frame but an invalid SUM command. The application grammar recognizes the uppercase token SUM followed by one to sixty-four decimal integers, each between minus one million and one million. Parsing uses the classic locale for token separation and from_chars for whole-token integer conversion. A leading plus sign is rejected by the chosen integer parser. Embedded zero bytes do not terminate the frame and make an otherwise numeric token invalid.

blocks.text: Application errors are framed responses: ERR command, ERR empty, ERR count, ERR value, or ERR size at the pure processor boundary. Transport errors instead terminate the connection and update a category counter. A network request declaring more than 4096 bytes is rejected at the framing boundary before the processor is called, so it does not receive a promise of an ERR size response.

blocks.text: The server defaults to two workers, four queued connections, and a one-second request budget. The budget starts when accept returns, not when a worker finally dequeues the connection. Queue delay therefore consumes the same request budget as reading, processing, and writing. A queued request already past its deadline fails when a worker begins its operation rather than receiving a fresh allowance.

blocks.text: Admission is nonblocking. A full or closed inbox rejects the newly accepted owned socket, whose destruction closes it. This is a resource policy, not a negotiated overload response protocol. At quiescence after joined shutdown, accepted connections equal admitted plus rejected, and admitted connections equal completed plus failed plus cancelled. Application-error responses are a subset of completed responses; timeouts are a subset of transport failures. Live snapshots use separate atomic loads and are not promised to form a simultaneous accounting snapshot.

topics.summary: The encoder and incremental decoder are independent of sockets and threads. They are used by deterministic split and boundary tests. Native receive uses the same declared length limit, while exact-transfer helpers deal with the operating system’s progress and termination behavior.

blocks.text: The decoder retains only a four-byte header and a payload bounded by the accepted length. A completed decoder consumes no bytes from a subsequent frame. If an allocation or parsing error occurs during feed, the decoder enters a failed state rather than offering an ambiguous partial result. The payload accessor is borrowed; copy the returned string if it must outlive the decoder.

topics.title: C.3 Bounded admission queue
topics.summary: The inbox uses a mutex and predicate wait for consumers, but producers use try_push and never wait for space. It drains accepted owners after closure. During server cancellation, workers still pop those owners, immediately observe stop in their operation, classify cancellation, and release the descriptors. This keeps accepted-item accounting explicit.

topics.title: C.4 Native ownership and operation state
topics.summary: An operation carries one absolute steady-clock deadline and an optional stop-state pointer. The pointer is borrowed from server state that outlives every worker. Native errors preserve a category and, where applicable, the original error number. The descriptor owner closes once under the Linux policy and preserves surrounding errno during destructor cleanup.

blocks.text: The adapter creates nonblocking sockets, handles partial transfer progress, retries interrupted operations, and waits after temporary unavailability. Polling uses at most twenty-five-millisecond slices to revisit stop and deadline state. Ready events are followed by actual I/O; a readiness flag alone is not interpreted as a complete message. Calls are chunked to a modest maximum rather than passing an arbitrarily large span length directly to the native interface.

blocks.text: A final progress check can report a deadline after a write has already submitted bytes. That is intentional: the program does not pretend it can retract an external effect. The client may have received some or all of a response even when the server records a late failure. Exactly-once transactional semantics would require another protocol. Time checks are cooperative observations subject to scheduling, not a proof of worst-case operating-system latency.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix C — HarborRelay: A Bounded, Cancellable Loopback Service
topics.title: C.5 Server ownership and supervision
topics.summary: The server owns its listener, stop state, inbox, counters, workers, and acceptor. It cannot be copied or moved because running threads reference its stable address. Only the supervising thread calls joined shutdown or destroys the object. Stop can be requested through the documented thread-safe path; a failure stored by the acceptor is inspected only after that thread has joined.

blocks.text: Construction validates configuration, creates the listener, starts workers, and finally starts the acceptor. A controlled test seam can fail before a selected worker launch. The constructor’s failure path closes the inbox and joins workers before their referenced members are destroyed. The ordinary command-line program never enables the seam.

The constructor’s failure path closes the inbox and joins workers before their referenced members are destroyed. The ordinary command-line program never enables the seam.

blocks.text: Per-connection failures stay inside the worker loop. Fatal failures of basic synchronization operations are outside the application’s recovery model; the noexcept worker boundary is not a claim that arbitrary mutex-runtime failure can be recovered. An acceptor failure records its exception, requests stop, and closes the inbox. The supervisor can then join and rethrow that preserved failure.

topics.summary: The test executable selects named cases so each CTest result has a clear scope. Pure grammar and framing tests are distinct from native transfer tests and complete server tests. Socket pairs exercise controlled stream behavior without external networking. Loopback clients exercise the real listener, admission path, workers, processor, and response adapter.

blocks.text: The deadline tests check an idle operation and a previously expired absolute deadline even when data is available. They do not assert a particular scheduler-level response time. The parallel-client case uses enough configured queue capacity for its finite batch and verifies response identity after joining clients. The smoke and parallel cases observe server completion before requesting stop: a client can receive bytes before the worker finishes its counter update or final cancellation check. A separate immediate-stop case accepts the documented terminal categories and verifies accounting rather than falsely ordering server bookkeeping through the client receive. The inbox case tests deterministic rejection directly instead of requiring a particular incidental rejection count from a network burst.

topics.summary: The implemented contract includes bounded frames, whole-token arithmetic validation, unique descriptor ownership, selected loopback ports, nonblocking transfer progress, shared absolute request deadlines, bounded admission, and joined stop. Tests cover malformed payloads, fragmented and truncated frames, maximum and oversized lengths, empty frames, cancellation, idle clients, no-client shutdown, parallel clients, invalid configuration, and partial worker startup failure.

blocks.text: The remaining production questions are not answered by these tests. Decide how peers are authenticated, how transport is encrypted, how overload is communicated, how the process is supervised, how logs and metrics are retained, how configuration changes are rolled back, and what service-level deadline policy applies across retries. A completed local test suite is the beginning of an operational review, not a substitute for it.
